# AMB009 amb-restart-stateful

A `restart` policy covers an impl in a stateful node that has no flow to a store.

## What it does

A node is stateful when it carries `attr stateful;` (grmb-spec has no richer surface form yet, so this attribute is the declaration). When a `restart` action (including an `else` fallback) of the system policy, or of the scenario override for an impl's scenario, covers an impl placed `in node` such a node, and no `flow` runs from that node to a node of `kind store`, the policy is flagged once per policy and node.

## Why it matters

Restarting a stateful node discards state that nothing persisted, so the recovery silently loses data.

## Remedy

Declare a flow from the node to a store, or use a policy other than `restart`.

## Examples

### Fires case 1

```grmb expect=fire file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

node mcu : trusted { attr stateful; }

system s {
  ambient restart max 2 { verified_by "tests/a.py"; }
  actor u : human;
  step u.go;
  step system.work;
  scenario t {
    u.go -> system.work => {
      ok -> end ok;
    }
  }
  impl system.work for t {
    in node mcu;
  }
}
```

### Clean case 2

```grmb expect=clean file=design/model.grmb
grimble = "2";
module m;

node mcu : trusted { attr stateful; }
node db : trusted { kind store; }
flow save : mcu -> db { label Internal; }

system s {
  ambient restart max 2 { verified_by "tests/a.py"; }
  actor u : human;
  step u.go;
  step system.work;
  scenario t {
    u.go -> system.work => {
      ok -> end ok;
    }
  }
  impl system.work for t {
    in node mcu;
  }
}
```
